intro: Biggest rank disagreements between the SEI board and SP+, 2026 season: from the SP+ top 15 and from our own top 15.

teams.explanation: Widest gap on the board by a mile. SP+ sees a Sun Belt middle-of-the-pack team - offense No. 48, defense No. 59 - after road losses of 45-14 at LSU and 36-19 at Baylor. SEI is buying the takeaways: opponent fumble rate (+2.32) and interception rate (+2.28) both sit at the 99th percentile, with a +1.51 stuff rate on top. SP+'s points-based engine treats that as variance, and one-score wins over Army (31-29) and Louisiana (32-31) keep it skeptical. SEI thinks the strip-and-steal profile is real skill.

SP+ rates Tech's offense No. 6; SEI has it No. 48, and the process profile backs SEI: no offensive metric clears +0.95 z on the season. A 53-48 win at West Virginia and a 52-27 win at Oklahoma State bracket the same attack - it scores a lot rather than efficiently. The one genuinely elite offensive-adjacent trait is takeaways (INT rate +2.07), which SP+'s points engine rewards more than weighted PPA does. Defense roughly agrees, SEI No. 20 to SP+ No. 33; the entire gap is the offense.
hints: Offense drives the gap: SEI off #48 vs def #20.

teams.explanation: Nebraska lost four straight in the fall - 20-17 to Indiana, 17-14 to Oregon, 17-10 to Washington, 24-13 to Illinois - and SP+ priced those losses in. SEI still sees a top-20 profile both ways: third-down pass PPA of +2.26 on defense and +1.83 on offense, red-zone TD% +1.52, capped by a 31-28 win over Ohio State. SP+ agrees on the defense (No. 9) but rates the offense 40th versus SEI's 25th. Penalties are the exception: offensive penalty rate z -2.25, nearly the worst nationally.
hints: Strongest metrics: 3rd pass PPA +2.26, 3rd pass PPA +1.83, RZ TD% +1.52.

teams.explanation: Both boards put Miami's offense at No. 1 - points per drive +2.78 at the 100th percentile, third-down pass PPA +2.57, explosiveness +2.23. The disagreement is the other side of the ball: SEI ranks the defense 43rd, SP+ 26th. Miami's defensive process profile has no elite entry, with stuff rate (-1.38) and havoc (-0.94) the most negative marks. North Carolina got to within three (38-35) before the only loss, at Notre Dame 31-24. SEI won't rank a 43rd-ranked defense third overall.
hints: Defense drives the gap: SEI off #1 vs def #43.
Strongest metrics: Pts/drive +2.78, 3rd pass PPA +2.57, Exp +2.23.

teams.explanation: The boards already agree this is a top-five defense - No. 1 for SEI, No. 5 for SP+ - built on red-zone TD% allowed +2.52, early-down rush PPA +2.02 and defensive points per drive +1.93. The gap is the scoreboard's shape: six of ten games were decided by one score, including 24-23 over Ohio State, 22-21 over LSU, and three-point losses to Oklahoma and Florida. SP+ compresses close-win teams; SEI's weighted components don't care that those games were coin flips, only that the process was dominant.
hints: Offense drives the gap: SEI off #24 vs def #1.
Strongest metrics: RZ TD% +2.52, Early rush PPA +2.02, Pts/drive +1.93.
6 of 10 games decided by <=7 pts (SP+ penalizes close wins harder than SEI does).

teams.explanation: Six and five, but SEI has LSU at No. 4 because the process is elite: third-down pass PPA +3.14 - first nationally - red-zone TD% +2.70, havoc +2.61 and sack rate +2.52 on a defense SP+ also places in the top ten. The losses are coin flips - 35-34 at Kentucky, 21-22 to Texas, eight at Ole Miss; only Alabama (31-13) and Tennessee (27-13) were lopsided. Ball security is the blemish (fumble z -1.51). SP+ sees 6-5 and a +111 margin; SEI sees 9-2 that didn't happen.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #22 (margin +111) but SEI #4.
Strongest metrics: 3rd pass PPA +3.14, RZ TD% +2.70, Havoc +2.61.

teams.explanation: SP+ trusts eleven wins more than SEI does. SP+'s offense ranks fourth; SEI's says 16th, and the components explain the discount: stuffed rate z -2.01 - stopped behind the line of scrimmage more than 96% of teams - plus interceptions (INT% -1.38). What's real is short-yardage rushing: third-down rush PPA +2.20, early-down +1.73. Defense is a wash between the boards (No. 23 versus No. 26). A 40-39 win at Arizona sums it up: SP+ reads the undefeated record, SEI reads how close the games were.
hints: Strongest metrics: 3rd rush PPA +2.20, Early rush PPA +1.73, INT% +1.65.
